description: E001 meets the reported date, public gathering, attendance and own-state demand criteria, but both opened reports are organizer/movement-adjacent. Police obstruction is mentioned without enough detail to code a response type.
required_followup: Independent contemporary coverage and fuller response/episode follow-up.

description: A December CIVICUS overview describes the Seibu workers’ strike as November 2024. The specific search follow-up for the named Seibu/Ikebukuro event returned Japan Times reports with 2023 dates and a 31 August 2023 event. The 2023 lead is excluded; no 2024 event was inferred from the discrepancy.
required_followup: If the claimed November 2024 strike refers to a different event, locate its specific source and date; do not transfer the 2023 attendance or labor action.

description: The monthly search returned a government-site page for a 23 November public meeting demanding the return of abductees. The captured result gives no attendance, protester character, or own-state demand; it was not coded as an event.
required_followup: Open only after a fresh exact-URL access check and manual review if the meeting is pursued; determine whether it was a public protest and whom participants demanded action from.

description: Five recorded searches included Japanese and English full-month terms, national labor/political terms and follow-up on the Hibiya rally and Seibu false lead. Open-web search is not LexisNexis; local source and newspaper archive coverage is incomplete. Historical source ledgers and official baseline are unavailable. Native search clocks were not exposed.
required_followup: Continue additional prefectural/sector searches or consult archives if available; reviewers should assess the limited source corpus.
